Job Summary

Associate Geospatial Analyst / Geospatial Analyst / Senior Geospatial Analyst

Map Data. Drive Decisions. Shape the Future.

Are you someone who sees the world in layers—of data, design, and discovery? Do you enjoy transforming information into robust planning, infrastructure, and public service tools? El Paso County is seeking a talented Geospatial Professional to join our Department of Public Works team and help build smarter, more connected communities through innovative GIS and asset management.

This is a career progression opportunity, with openings at the Associate, Analyst, and Senior Analyst levels.
Whether you're just starting your geospatial journey or are a seasoned GIS pro, there’s a place for you here to grow and make an impact.

What You’ll Do

As part of the Geospatial Analyst team, you’ll be key in maintaining and analyzing asset data for transportation systems, public infrastructure, and County resources. You’ll support everything from road maintenance planning and crash data analysis to field data collection and custom map development.
Your work will support day-to-day operations, long-term infrastructure planning, and innovative solutions that make our county run more efficiently. From scripting and database development to GIS app creation and stakeholder collaboration, your expertise will help power decisions that matter.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You have strong technical skills in GIS, asset management systems, and data analysis.
You’re fluent in tools like ArcGIS, SQL, Python, ModelBuilder, and GIS dashboards.
You can turn raw spatial data into actionable insights, maps, and visuals.
You’re a collaborative problem-solver who enjoys working with cross-functional teams.
You have a passion for public service and building tools that improve communities.
You're adaptable, self-motivated, and thrive in a fast-paced, detail-driven environment.

Why Join El Paso County?

Your Work Has Meaning – Help plan and maintain the infrastructure that residents rely on every day.
Room to Grow – Our career progression path means your role grows as your skills do.
Use the Latest Tools – Get hands-on experience with cutting-edge GIS, programming, and asset management systems.
Collaborate Across Departments – Work closely with engineers, planners, field staff, and local agencies.
Be Part of a Mission-Driven Team – We’re passionate about service, innovation, and supporting each other.

We want to hear from you if you’re ready to map your career forward and contribute to impactful projects that shape El Paso County’s future.

Apply today to be part of a geospatial team where your skills and ideas truly make a difference!

jobs.title: Grants Administrator / Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Grants Administrator/Compliance Analyst provides administration and oversight for grant awards for the City of Pocatello to ensure funds are used in compliance with grant requirements and that the City is compliant with all applicable local, state, and federal laws.

The job requires knowledge of related applicable federal and state grant program administrative requirements, attention to details and knowledge of accounting and bookkeeping methods. The job requires the ability to maintain a collaborative and cooperative working relationship with elected and appointed officials, other City employees, other organizations, and the general public.

The job requires extensive knowledge of federal regulations, including the Office of Management and Budget Uniform Guidance, 2 CFR 200.

The work environment is a department office environment. The job occasionally requires field inspections of projects under construction. The noise level is generally moderate.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Administers federal funds to ensure the City is compliant with federal laws on grant funding and disbursement. Monitors spending by sub-recipients, contractors, and other agencies for grant compliance.
Prepares and processes complex funding, draw requests, reviews financial documentation, and manages contracts with sub-recipients, contractors, agencies, and other funders to ensure compliance with grant stipulations. Verifies funding is received and disbursed by the City.
Prepares and maintains records, documents, and logs all in accordance with City, State, and Federal record retention requirements. Prepares required reports on grant compliance. Performs on-side inspections to ensure compliance, as needed.
Administers components of grant-funded projects included the CDBG RENEWAL loan program. Assists with the review of applicants for the CDBG RENEWAL grant and sidewalk program, including eligibility of applicants, proper scopes of work, procurement for services, and contract oversight. Reviews applications, reviews recommendations by Grant Division Staff, assists in determining eligibility and prepares loan applications and documents. Serves as the CDBG RENEWAL loan program Loan Officer.
Assists in the review of sub-recipient applications for funding. Reviews applications, assists in determining eligibility, and assists with the CDBG Advisory Committee’s review of HUD-funded subrecipient applications.
Reviews applications, assists in determining eligibility and assists with the CDBG Advisory Committee’s review.
Conducts monitoring (audits) of subrecipients in compliance with all federal regulations and requirements, including eligibility of clients serves or activities completed, allowability and allocability of expenditures, record retention, and uniform guidance requirements. Conducts internal monitoring of federally funded grant awards to ensure City compliance with all regulations and requirements. Develops corrective action plans for subrecipients or other monitored entities, including the City, to ensure compliance with all regulations.
Assists with creation of bid documents and construction bids for the public facility and other funded construction projects; reviews these documents and bids for grant compliance. Administers federal wage compliance regulations (Davis-Bacon) on construction projects. Ensures compliance with Davis-Bacon Wage Act requirements, including on-site monitoring and wage rate sheet reviews. Serves as the City’s Labor Standards Officer for Davis-Bacon Wage Act.
Ensures compliance with all procurement requirements for federal, state, and locally funded grant projects.
Assists with conducting grant compliance training for City staff. Maintains written policies and procedures required by grant awards are compliant with requirements and updates policies and procedures as needed. These policies may include Grant Policies and Procedures, Conflict of Interest Policies, grant-specific Purchase/Procurement Policies, Inventory Policy, Monitoring Policy, Cybersecurity Policy, Language Assistance Plan, Nondiscrimination Policy, and Title VI Plan, among others.
Completes required reporting including programmatic, performance and finance reports for grant-funded projects.
Responsible for ensuring compliance with applicable local, state, and federal record retention requirements.
Performs all work duties and activities in accordance with City policies, procedures, and safety practices.
Performs other duties as assigned. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this position at any time.

Acceptable Experience, Training, Licenses And/Or Certifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Public or Business Administration, accounting or finance, or related field is required;
At least two (2) years grant administration and/or loan-processing experience is preferred;
Idaho driver’s license is required.

An equivalent combination of education and experience that provides the required skills, knowledge, and abilities to successfully perform the essential functions of the position may be considered.

Classification Requirements

The requirements listed below are representative of the minimum knowledge, skill, and/or ability required for an individual to satisfactorily perform each essential duty and be successful in the position.

Knowledge Of

Federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and other applicable and related federal grant and program administrative requirements, methods, techniques, and objectives;
Procurement and purchasing policies for local, state, and federal entities;
Federal Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200;
Intermediate accounting and bookkeeping methods, techniques, and objectives;
Methods and techniques of loan qualifying and processing;
Contract oversight and project management;
Operation of basic office equipment including a personal computer and job-related software applications.

Skill And Ability To

Process monthly draws on grant fund accounts to ensure compliance with grant requirements and stipulations;
Process loan applications to determine if applications of complete and eligible for CDBG funding, requesting further documentation as needed;
Prepare annual funding requests for presentation to City Council or Advisory Committee for review and action;
Prepare and maintain records, documents, and logs and prepare periodic reports;
Prepare and reconcile financial reports and records in accordance with Federal program requirements;
Interpret, understand, and implement complex federal, state, and local regulations and requirements;
Demonstrate strong customer service principles including issue resolution;
Maintain a collaborative and cooperative working relationship with elected and appointed officials, other City employees, and the public;
Communicate effectively in the English language at a level necessary for efficient job performance;
Complete assignments in a timely fashion; understand and comply with all rules, policies, and regulations;
Perform all duties in accordance with City policies and procedures with regard to personal safety and that of other employees and the public.

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel, bend, use hands to handle materials, manipulate tools, keyboard and type, reach with hands and arms, and operate job-related equipment. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds with assistance. Sufficient visual acuity and hearing capacity to perform the essential functions and interact with the public is required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

DISCLAIMER

The above statements describe the general nature, level, and type of work performed by the incumbent(s) assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, demands, and skills required of personnel so classified. Job descriptions are not intended to and do not imply or create any employment, compensation, or contract rights to any person or persons. Management reserves the right to add, delete, or modify any and/or all provisions of this description at any time as needed without notice. This job description supersedes earlier versions.

Medical
Prescription

PERSI Retirement
PERSI Choice 401(k)
457 Retirement Planning

Nestled in the foothills of the majestic Rocky Mountains, Pocatello offers a perfect blend of work and play. With a semi-arid climate, you can experience the best of all four seasons, from hiking and skiing to fishing and camping. Plus, you're just a short drive away from Yellowstone National Park, Grand Teton National Park, Lava Hot Springs, and other must-visit destinations.

jobs.description:
At Ripple, we’re building a world where value moves like information does today. It’s big, it’s bold, and we’re already doing it. Through our crypto solutions for financial institutions, businesses, governments and developers, we are improving the global financial system and creating greater economic fairness and opportunity for more people, in more places around the world. And we get to do the best work of our career and grow our skills surrounded by colleagues who have our backs. 
If you’re ready to see your impact and unlock incredible career growth opportunities, join us, and build real world value.
THE WORK:

The Customer Success Manager plays a key role in driving revenue, product adoption and retention across the Ripple Treasury customer base in EMEA. Acting as a trusted advisor to Heads of Treasury, Finance leaders and CFOs, the CSM will own a portfolio of strategic enterprise accounts — deepening relationships, accelerating adoption of Ripple Treasury's cash, liquidity, forecasting, payments, netting, reconciliation capabilities, and supporting expansion and renewal opportunities across Ripple's product suite
WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Own a portfolio of strategic enterprise treasury accounts across EMEA, with responsibility for adoption, retention, satisfaction and growth outcomes.
Develop a deep understanding of each customer's treasury organisation, technical landscape, internal decision-making, aspirations and needs — mapping their workflows to measurable success outcomes on the Ripple Treasury platform.
Build trusted, senior-level relationships with Heads of Treasury, Finance leaders and CFOs, serving as an advisor and Ripple advocate.
Run QBRs and executive-level success reviews; conduct financial, business and value analysis tied to customer targets such as cost reduction, forecasting accuracy and operational efficiency.
Own the commercial health of your portfolio: maintain an early-warning view of churn risk (health scores, usage decline, escalations, sentiment), flag at-risk accounts to AM/RM with a documented save plan, and build account strategies that identify and progress renewal, upsell and cross-sell opportunities through to deal execution.
Champion the innovation and product agenda across your book of business, turning each release into measurable customer adoption.
Drive customer references and advocacy across the portfolio, building a pipeline of referenceable accounts and advocacy assets (case studies, testimonials, event speakers…) in partnership with Marketing.
Lead and support customer events across the EMEA region, driving engagement and community-building within your book of business.
Resolve complex product and operational issues by partnering with Support, Engineering and Technical Services, and by leading deep root-cause analysis where required.
Represent the voice of the customer across Ripple; collect and communicate customer feedback to Product, Engineering and GTM to shape the roadmap.
Maintain admin and operational excellence across your book of business, keeping account data and response SLAs at a consistently high standard.

Identify and champion internal process improvements.

Fluency in English is required; German and/or French are a plus.
4+ years of experience in customer-facing roles within enterprise SaaS, FinTech or financial services, ideally in Customer Success or strategic account management.
Deep domain expertise in corporate treasury: cash and liquidity management, cash flow forecasting, netting, payments and settlement, bank connectivity… — hands-on practitioner experience in a corporate treasury function is a strong plus.
Direct experience with Treasury Management Systems (e.g. Ripple Treasury, Kyriba, IT2, Quantum, or similar), as an implementer, power user or vendor-side advisor.

Experience running QBRs and executive business reviews, and conducting value and business analysis against customer financial targets.

jobs.title: Assistant Planner
jobs.description:
About Grocery Outlet

Our Mission:
Touching lives for the better

Our Vision:
Touching lives by being the first choice for bargain-minded consumers in the U.S.

Our Values & Behaviors:
Achievement, Diversity, Entrepreneurship, Family, Fun, Integrity & Service

About The Team

Our Planning team’s mission is to constantly push the status quo to deliver the best service to our buying team and store operators. Our team is highly intelligent and engaged with the business- allowing us to operate in a fast-paced environment and form cross-functional partnerships. Successful members of our team maximize profitability and productivity within their department and motivate their team and cross functional partners with their energy.

About The Role

You will be responsible for managing the distribution of merchandise to support company plan. Extremely “hands-on”, you will need to be able to make quick decisions, manage key warehouse and planning relationships and provide inventory information for your assigned departments. You will be responsible for assisting the Planning Team in ensuring proper product inventories at all stores to facilitate optimum code life, minimize seasonal markdowns and maximize turns. You will recommend and execute changes as needed to ensure profitability and productivity. You will also maximize sales potential by performing the following duties: The Assistant Planner will report to the Sr. Inventory Planner.

Responsibilities Include

Understand and execute appropriate distribution of products to stores to maximize store turns and profitability
Implement the company’s "Treasure Hunt" philosophy and merchandise assortment strategy through effective execution of product allocation to stores
Analyze store level data to identify chain/region/store level trends and recommend/implement changes and action as appropriate
Execute category/sub-class trends regionally and identify specific merchandise needs through knowledge of regional and climatic characteristics
Execute seasonal distributions in accordance with direction provided by planning & purchasing teams
Responsible for managing those items approaching expiration in the warehouse
Responsible for managing items on the Aged report (slower moving items – identify and collaborate with planner, action as appropriate)
Responsible for building, in partnership with set crew, an appropriate inventory mix to support new store openings
Manage store distribution groups based on location, volume, size, demographics and sales trends
Own cross-functional communication regarding product sales, inventory position, and distributions for all stores

jobs.description:
Customer Success Specialist
Location:
Remote, U.S. (Pacific Time Zone Preferred)

About Knomee
Knomee is building the behavioral intelligence platform for financial services.
We help financial institutions drive organic growth by understanding what clients and prospects want, what’s changing, and when they’re ready to act. Our platform combines behavioral science, AI, and thoughtful product design to help firms convert prospects, deepen relationships, grow households, and retain clients through transitions.

We're an early-stage company creating a new category. Every customer matters. Every implementation teaches us something. Every successful customer helps us build a better company.
We're looking for our first Customer Success Specialist to help customers adopt Knomee, realize value quickly, and become long-term advocates. 

The Opportunity

As Knomee's first Customer Success Specialist, you'll work directly with the CEO to ensure every customer has an exceptional experience—from onboarding through adoption, renewal, and expansion.
You'll become the primary point of contact for our customers, helping them achieve meaningful outcomes while serving as the voice of the customer inside the company. You'll identify what's working, where customers get stuck, and how we can continuously improve.

This is a hands-on, high-energy role for someone who wants to build, not inherit, a customer success playbook. You’ll be close to our customers from day one, constantly testing creative ways to increase engagement and usage. If you’re looking for established processes and predictable days, this probably isn’t the right fit. If you want significant responsibility early in your career and the chance to figure out what works, it could be.

What You'll Own
You'll own the day-to-day customer experience and help build the foundation of Knomee's customer success function.

Specifically, you will:
Lead customer onboarding and help customers get to value quickly.
Engage customers proactively at least weekly with ideas, use cases, templates, insights, and recommendations that give them reasons to use Knomee.
Own activation and usage. If engagement is low, dig into why, develop a hypothesis, try something, and measure whether it worked.
Build trusted relationships with advisors and customer stakeholders.
Learn how each customer grows and find creative ways to embed Knomee into their existing marketing, business development, advisor, and client workflows.
Own weekly customer success reporting, tracking logins, usage, invitations, completions, use cases, risks, and actions so we always know what’s working, what isn’t, and what we’re doing next.
Support pilots, renewals, and expansion opportunities.
Turn successful experiments and customer learnings into templates, best practices, and repeatable playbooks that help every customer get more value from Knomee.
Bring customer feedback and patterns back to Product and Engineering.
Jump in wherever needed to make a customer successful. At our stage, no customer task is beneath you.

How Success Is Measured
Success in this role is measured by customer outcomes—not activity. 
Your success will be reflected in:
Customer activation and time-to-value
Weekly and monthly active usage
Growth in Knomee invitations and completions
Adoption of high-value use cases
Pilot-to-contract conversion, retention, and expansion
Customer outcomes tied to growth
Your ability to turn experiments into repeatable activation playbooks

If customers aren't realizing value from Knomee, we haven't succeeded. If usage is low, your job is not simply to report it. Your job is to understand why and figure out what we can do about it.

What We're Looking For
We're looking for someone who enjoys working with customers, takes ownership naturally, and thrives in a fast-moving environment. In any given week, you might analyze usage data, call customers, create an engagement campaign, test a new activation idea, and report back on what worked. You won't wait for a playbook. You'll help us build it.
You likely bring:
1–4 years of professional experience, ideally in Customer Success, Account Management, Implementation, Sales, consulting, fintech, or another customer-facing role.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
Comfort with data and the discipline to measure whether your work is changing customer behavior.
Strong organization and attention to detail.
Comfort communicating directly with senior customers despite being earlier in your career.
Genuine belief in what Knomee is building and enthusiasm for helping customers see its value.

Experience in wealth management, fintech, or enterprise SaaS is a very major plus.

How You Work

You are:
Hungry to learn and prove yourself.
High-energy, optimistic, and persistent.
Resourceful when there isn't an obvious answer.
Willing to do the detailed, repetitive work required to get something right.
Curious about customers and why people behave the way they do.
Someone who sees “we don't have a playbook yet” as an opportunity, not a problem.

You don't expect someone else to solve problems first. You identify what needs to happen, take initiative, and follow through.

You don't confuse a customer saying they like Knomee with customer success. Success means they are using it, getting measurable value from it, and wanting to use it more.

Growth Opportunity
This role is the foundation of Knomee's customer success function.
As the company grows, strong performance will create opportunities to take on broader ownership across customer success, enterprise implementations, account expansion, and team leadership. Growth will be based on demonstrated impact—not tenure.

Why Join Knomee
We believe the future of financial services is more human. Join us in building the behavioral intelligence layer that helps financial institutions understand people better and turn that understanding into growth.

Email careers@knomee.com with your cover letter and resume.

Job Description

The Grants Administrator/Compliance Analyst provides administration and oversight for grant awards for the City of Pocatello to ensure funds are used in compliance with grant requirements and that the City is compliant with all applicable local, state, and federal laws.

The job requires knowledge of related applicable federal and state grant program administrative requirements, attention to details and knowledge of accounting and bookkeeping methods. The job requires the ability to maintain a collaborative and cooperative working relationship with elected and appointed officials, other City employees, other organizations, and the general public.

The job requires extensive knowledge of federal regulations, including the Office of Management and Budget Uniform Guidance, 2 CFR 200.

The work environment is a department office environment. The job occasionally requires field inspections of projects under construction. The noise level is generally moderate.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Administers federal funds to ensure the City is compliant with federal laws on grant funding and disbursement. Monitors spending by sub-recipients, contractors, and other agencies for grant compliance.
Prepares and processes complex funding, draw requests, reviews financial documentation, and manages contracts with sub-recipients, contractors, agencies, and other funders to ensure compliance with grant stipulations. Verifies funding is received and disbursed by the City.
Prepares and maintains records, documents, and logs all in accordance with City, State, and Federal record retention requirements. Prepares required reports on grant compliance. Performs on-side inspections to ensure compliance, as needed.
Administers components of grant-funded projects included the CDBG RENEWAL loan program. Assists with the review of applicants for the CDBG RENEWAL grant and sidewalk program, including eligibility of applicants, proper scopes of work, procurement for services, and contract oversight. Reviews applications, reviews recommendations by Grant Division Staff, assists in determining eligibility and prepares loan applications and documents. Serves as the CDBG RENEWAL loan program Loan Officer.
Assists in the review of sub-recipient applications for funding. Reviews applications, assists in determining eligibility, and assists with the CDBG Advisory Committee’s review of HUD-funded subrecipient applications.
Reviews applications, assists in determining eligibility and assists with the CDBG Advisory Committee’s review.
Conducts monitoring (audits) of subrecipients in compliance with all federal regulations and requirements, including eligibility of clients serves or activities completed, allowability and allocability of expenditures, record retention, and uniform guidance requirements. Conducts internal monitoring of federally funded grant awards to ensure City compliance with all regulations and requirements. Develops corrective action plans for subrecipients or other monitored entities, including the City, to ensure compliance with all regulations.
Assists with creation of bid documents and construction bids for the public facility and other funded construction projects; reviews these documents and bids for grant compliance. Administers federal wage compliance regulations (Davis-Bacon) on construction projects. Ensures compliance with Davis-Bacon Wage Act requirements, including on-site monitoring and wage rate sheet reviews. Serves as the City’s Labor Standards Officer for Davis-Bacon Wage Act.
Ensures compliance with all procurement requirements for federal, state, and locally funded grant projects.
Assists with conducting grant compliance training for City staff. Maintains written policies and procedures required by grant awards are compliant with requirements and updates policies and procedures as needed. These policies may include Grant Policies and Procedures, Conflict of Interest Policies, grant-specific Purchase/Procurement Policies, Inventory Policy, Monitoring Policy, Cybersecurity Policy, Language Assistance Plan, Nondiscrimination Policy, and Title VI Plan, among others.
Completes required reporting including programmatic, performance and finance reports for grant-funded projects.
Responsible for ensuring compliance with applicable local, state, and federal record retention requirements.
Performs all work duties and activities in accordance with City policies, procedures, and safety practices.
Performs other duties as assigned. Nothing in this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this position at any time.

Acceptable Experience, Training, Licenses And/Or Certifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Public or Business Administration, accounting or finance, or related field is required;
At least two (2) years grant administration and/or loan-processing experience is preferred;
Idaho driver’s license is required.

An equivalent combination of education and experience that provides the required skills, knowledge, and abilities to successfully perform the essential functions of the position may be considered.

Federal Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200;
